Fresh floods and landslides set off by heavy rain and storms have killed at least 14 people in Nepal and left another 11 missing, with authorities warning on Sunday that more flash floods were possible. The warnings covered 49 of Nepal's 77 districts, more than half of which faced a high risk of flooding, as water levels in major rivers kept rising. The video filmed at 5:30pm, local time, on Sunday, September 27 shows the latest destruction. Pemandangan mengerikan terjadi di kawasan dekat Kota Lete, Mustang, Nepal. Bagian lereng gunung runtuh dan memicu longsoran besar yang menutupi sebagian aliran Sungai Kali Gandaki serta merusak sejumlah jalan di sekitarnya. Dalam video amatir yang beredar, material berupa debu dan bebatuan terlihat meluncur deras dari lereng seperti air terjun. Di tengah kepulan debu, sejumlah tiang jaringan listrik masih terlihat berdiri. Longsor tersebut disebut terjadi di tengah hujan monsun ekstrem yang melanda sejumlah wilayah Nepal. Meski longsor di kawasan Lete dilaporkan tidak menimbulkan korban jiwa, bencana hidrometeorologi di sejumlah wilayah Nepal dilaporkan telah menyebabkan korban meninggal dunia dan memaksa ratusan warga mengungsi.(yn) 📹 : istimewa #peristiwa #longsor #gunung #mustang #nepal

🚨 SOMETHING UNUSUAL IS HAPPENING IN NEPAL 🇳🇵 Multiple mountainsides and hillsides have collapsed across Nepal in recent days, with terrifying footage showing entire sections of terrain giving way within seconds. The latest incidents come after days of heavy rainfall, flooding and landslides across several districts. At least 24 people have reportedly died and 14 remain missing in the latest wave of flooding and landslides. (NDTV) But one question is spreading online: 🌋 Is this part of a larger geological event — or are these separate landslides being triggered by the extreme weather? Scientists have previously linked major Himalayan collapses to a combination of geological conditions, rainfall, glacier instability and climate-related changes. However, there is currently no confirmed evidence that the latest collapses are one single coordinated geological event. (Newcastle University) ⚠️ Nepal remains on high alert as heavy rain continues to trigger flooding, landslides and avalanches. Nepal’s youngest prime minister Balendra Shah told world leaders at the UN that Nepal’s latest flash floods that killed more than 1,400 people are a “close warning for humanity,” and that action is needed now. On Aug. 26, deadly flash floods caused by a glacial collapse struck Nepal, sweeping through villages along the Nepal-Tibet border, killing more than 1,494 people and leaving more than 6,150 people missing. On Thursday, Sept. 24, Shah addressed the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in New York City for the first time. “The Bhotekoshi-Trishuli disaster was not just a local tragedy; it was a warning to the world. And I ask you today: have we really heard that warning?” Shah said. Shah recalled that UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned of an impending climate disaster at the foot of Mount Everest nearly three years ago, and called out world leaders for failing to act despite local communities and scientists reporting the effects of climate change He said climate change, as seen in the floods, affected people across Nepal and Tibet and will affect everyone. “Climate change does not recognize borders. Glaciers and floods do not travel with stamps on passports,” he said. Shah said that Nepal did not create the climate crisis, contributing less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, but is still paying a “colossal price.” According to Shah, Nepal would need to use 10% of its gross domestic product (GDP) to rebuild from the floods, adding that it cannot be constantly rebuilding. While Shah did not ask for financial aid, he told leaders that the Loss and Damage Fund, the Global Environment Facility and other financial mechanisms remain “grossly inadequate.” “Climate finance must not become another bureaucratic mess through which vulnerable countries spend years that they need help,” he said. “When the house is burning, we do not ask the family to complete 50 forms. We act.” Shah also called for cooperation between Nepal, India and China to improve climate resilience and disaster response across the Himalayas. #nepal #balendrashah #un #climate #fyp
